chunks.arabic_text: عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ، أَبُو الْقَاسِمِ، الْكُوفِيُّ، الْمُدَّعِي الْعَلَوِيَّةُ. كَاذِبٌ، غَالٍ، صَاحِبُ بِدْعَةٍ وَمَقَالَةٍ. رَأَيْتُ لَهُ كُتُبًا كَثِيرَةً، لَا يُلْتَفَتُ إِلَيْهِ.

translations.en: Ali ibn Ahmad, Abu al-Qasim, al-Kufi, the propagator of ghulw. A liar, a ghali, the possessor of a bid'ah and a doctrine. I saw he has many books, he is not turned to.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri’s *Kitab al-Duda'a* characterizes Ali ibn Ahmad al-Kufi as a prominent figure of the Ghulat (exaggerators) who, despite producing numerous works, is deemed unreliable due to his specific doctrinal innovations. His status as a 'liar' (kadhhab) in this context highlights the critical Shia methodology of distinguishing between mere narrators and those whose theological exaggerations compromised their authority in transmitting hadith.
en.seo_question: Who is Ali ibn Ahmad al-Kufi and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?
